_meta.indication: Management of neuropathic pain associated with postherpetic neuralgia (PHN).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, parallel-arm, multicenter, active-controlled study comparing a single 60-minute application of Qutenza 8% capsaicin patch to a low-concentration (3.2 mcg/cm2) control patch.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with moderate to severe postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) pain.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change from baseline in the “average pain for the past 24 hours” NPRS score during Weeks 2-8 (prespecified primary endpoint).
pivotal_trials.result: Percent change from baseline (Weeks 2-8): -29.6 Qutenza vs -19.9 control; difference 9.7, p=0.001.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, multicenter, active-controlled, parallel-arm study; single 60-minute application with 12-week efficacy assessments; low-concentration capsaicin control patch (3.2 mcg/cm2).
pivotal_trials.population: Adults aged 18-90 diagnosed with PHN and at least 6 months of pain since shingles vesicle crusting.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percent change in average pain from baseline to Weeks 2-8 (prespecified primary endpoint).
pivotal_trials.result: Percent change from baseline (Weeks 2-8): -32.0 Qutenza vs -24.4 control; difference 7.6, p=0.011.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5% and greater than control) are application site erythema (63% vs 54%), application site pain (42% vs 21%), application site pruritus (6% vs 4%), and application site papules (6% vs 3%). Warnings include application-associated pain and transient increases in blood pressure.
target_moa: Capsaicin is a highly selective agonist of the transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) receptor; following exposure, cutaneous nociceptors become less sensitive (“defunctionalization”), reducing spontaneous and evoked painful sensations.
modality: Small molecule (capsaicin) delivered as an 8% cutaneous patch.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held, as capsaicin has been marketed for many years, has well-defined adverse effects, limited absorption in this dosage form, trials clearly demonstrating efficacy, and no unexpected or concerning safety signals.

description.text: Added indication for treatment of neuropathic pain associated with diabetic peripheral neuropathy of the feet

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the following change: the addition of the indication for the treatment of neuropathic pain associated with diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) of the feet.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan-drug designation granted May 22, 2009 for “management of neuropathic pain in patients with post herpetic neuralgia.”

citations.quote: Pursuant to Section 526 of the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 360bb), the Applicant’s request for orphan-drug designation status was granted on May 22nd 2009 for “management of neuropathic pain in patients with post herpetic neuralgia”

summary.text: NDA 022395 was submitted under section 505(b)(2) for QUTENZA (capsaicin) 8% patch and underwent Standard review. The product received orphan-drug designation for PHN, which exempted it from PREA pediatric requirements. No advisory committee meeting was held. It was approved first cycle for management of neuropathic pain associated with postherpetic neuralgia.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated October 13, 2008, received October 16, 2008, submitted pursuant to section 505(b)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for QUTENZA™ (capsaicin) 8% patch.
Qutenza received orphan indication designation for PHN, thus the requirements of the Pediatric Research Equity Act do not apply. Furthermore, PHN is extremely rare in children.

An advisory committee meeting was not held for as capsaicin has been marketed for many years, has well-defined adverse effects, has limited absorption in this dosage form, trials clearly demonstrating efficacy and no unexpected or concerning safety signals.
